attempts.summary: Configured a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (node1/node2/node3, RHEL10, mariadb-server-galera 10.11.18) with firewall ports (3306/4567/4568/4444) and SELinux boolean mysql_connect_any opened for wsrep traffic. Bootstrapped on node1 via galera_new_cluster, joined node2 and node3 via rsync SST. Verified writes issued on any member replicate synchronously to the other two (multi-master). Tested availability during a single-member outage (stopped node2, wrote successfully from node1 and node3 with cluster_status=Primary at size 2) and automatic resynchronization when node2 rejoined (auto SST, back to size 3/Synced with all rows intact). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id + cluster health baseline on each node, restarted node1, node2, node3 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled each until reachable, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed each node returned to mariadb active / wsrep_cluster_size=3 / Synced / Primary with full data present before proceeding to the next node.
